Email is where life's to-do list actually arrives: the permission slip due
Friday, the dentist moved to Thursday, the flight confirmation, the bill, the
person waiting on a reply. Other mail apps help you *read* faster. **Chord does
the next step.** Every ask becomes a card beside its email. Tap, and it is on
your calendar, on your to-do list, answered, or gone.

**Nothing happens until you tap.** Chord suggests; you decide. It never sends,
deletes, books or shares on its own.

### Turn emails into action items

Chord reads each email and pulls out every separate thing it asks of you: a form to sign, a bill to pay, a date to keep, a person waiting on an answer. Each becomes a card in Action Items with the action ready to go.

- One email can hold several asks. A school newsletter with three dates gives you three cards.
- Cards sit beside the email they came from, and in one Action Items list across all your mailboxes.
- Marketing blasts, coupons and newsletters are left alone, so the list stays short.
- When an email changes something you already have (a cancellation, a new time), Chord offers to change it, not to add a second copy.

**In Claude or ChatGPT:** ask *“What's waiting on me in Chord?”* ([connect Chord](https://chordapp.ai/features/claude-and-chatgpt))

[More →](https://chordapp.ai/features/email-to-action-items)

### Add events from email to your calendar

Appointments, practices, school events, dinners and bookings become calendar events with the right date, time, place and time zone. Chord writes them to Google Calendar or Outlook, two-way synced.

- Reads the attached .ics file when there is one, so the time is exact.
- Puts a flight on the clock of its airport, not yours.
- Recognises when an invite and an earlier email are the same event, so nothing lands twice.
- Never adds a date that has already passed.
- Works with Google Calendar, Outlook calendars and your phone’s calendars.

**In Claude or ChatGPT:** ask *“Find the soccer email and add the next game to my calendar.”* ([connect Chord](https://chordapp.ai/features/claude-and-chatgpt))

[More →](https://chordapp.ai/features/email-to-calendar)

### An email to-do list that clears itself

A permission slip, a bill, an RSVP, a reply you owe: Chord turns each into a to-do with its deadline. When you reply to the email, the "reply to…" to-do finishes itself. When you delete the email, its to-do goes too.

- Deadlines come from the email. Chord never invents one.
- A "reply to Sarah" to-do is done the moment you reply, from Chord or any other mail app.
- Old to-dos that are past their date are archived, and the morning briefing tells you which and why.
- A sale or coupon is not a to-do. Chord only suggests things someone is actually waiting on.

### A morning briefing of your day and your inbox

Every morning, at the time you choose, Chord sends one summary: birthdays first, then today’s events, what is due, the emails waiting on you, and the weather. It arrives in the app and, if you like, on WhatsApp.

- Birthdays and anniversaries lead, from your people, calendar and mail.
- Today’s events, and clashes worth knowing about.
- To-dos that are due, and the ones Chord retired, named with the reason.
- Emails waiting on a reply, and a short list of what is worth a look.
- Weather for where you are.
- Leave out what you don’t want: "don’t include Rippling emails in my summary."
- Want it now? Say "send me my briefing".

### AI email replies that know when you are free

Tap Suggested and Chord drafts a reply from the whole thread. When the email asks about a time, Chord checks your calendar first: it confirms a time that works, or offers the closest free times inside your work hours.

- Availability is computed from your calendar, not guessed by the AI.
- Reads times on the writer’s clock, so "10:30 PT" is checked as 10:30 Pacific.
- Knows when you are away and will not offer an in-person meeting in another city.
- Skips weekends and holidays unless you say otherwise.
- Undo send, drafts that sync to your mail app, and your own signature.
- When an email asks several things, tap Point by point to answer each one in turn.

**In Claude or ChatGPT:** ask *“Draft a reply to the plumber saying Tuesday works.”* ([connect Chord](https://chordapp.ai/features/claude-and-chatgpt))

[More →](https://chordapp.ai/features/ai-email-replies)

### Reply with a time that matches what they asked

When an email asks "does Tuesday at 10:30 PT work?" or offers a few windows, Chord checks each one against your calendar on the writer’s own clock. If one is free, the reply says yes to it. If not, it offers the closest free times inside your work hours.

- Reads times in the sender’s time zone: "10:30 PT" is checked as 10:30 Pacific and shown on your clock too.
- Understands "tomorrow", "next Friday", "Tuesday or Wednesday morning" and ranges like "2–4 PM".
- Your free time is worked out from your calendar, not guessed by the AI.
- Stays inside your work hours and skips weekends and holidays, unless you set them differently.
- Knows when you are travelling and will not offer an in-person meeting in another city.
- Set your hours in chat: "my work hours are 8 to 4, Monday to Thursday."

**In Claude or ChatGPT:** ask *“Am I free Thursday afternoon? Suggest a time for coffee with Sam.”* ([connect Chord](https://chordapp.ai/features/claude-and-chatgpt))

### One-tap email summaries (tldr)

Every open email has a tldr button. Chord writes a few lines: what it is, who it is from, what it asks of you, and every date, amount and code as written.

- A short email gets one or two lines. A long one gets one line per action, deadline or decision.
- Dates, amounts and confirmation codes are quoted exactly.
- Only on request. Nothing is summarised unless you tap.

### Mass unsubscribe from mailing lists

Chord lists the mailing lists you are on, shows how many of their emails you actually opened, and lets you leave them all at once. For a list that will not let go, it sends their future mail straight to Trash.

- Honest about each one: "Unsubscribed", "Request sent" or "Finish on their page".
- Offers to leave a list you have ignored for weeks, at most once a day.

### Get to inbox zero and stay there

Once Chord has pulled the asks out of an email, the email itself can go. Swipe to archive or trash, clear many at once, snooze what can wait, and let rules file the rest into your own mailbox folders.

- Swipe to archive or move to Trash (you pick which), swipe the other way to mark read.
- Select many emails and archive or trash them together.
- Snooze an email until later today, tomorrow or next week.
- Filing rules in plain words: "always put mail from the PTA in my School folder". Mail moves to a real folder in your Gmail, Outlook or IMAP mailbox.
- "Send future mail to Trash" for senders that keep mailing after you leave their list.

### Spot phishing, fake senders and spam

Chord checks every email you open: a bank name on a free-mail address, a look-alike domain, a failed authentication check, a reply address somewhere else. It warns you in plain words and strips links from a likely fake.

- Catches look-alike domains, hidden characters in the sender name and brand names on the wrong domain.
- Warns before you reply to an address that is not the brand.
- Never suggests a to-do or a call from a suspicious email.
- Remote images load through Chord, so senders cannot see where you are.
- Mail in Spam never becomes a to-do or an event, and anything already suggested from an email is withdrawn when it lands in Spam.
- Suspected spam is never saved on your phone.

## Your mail stays yours

- **Nothing happens until you tap.** Chord suggests; you decide. It never sends, deletes, books or shares on its own. Every event, to-do, reply and unsubscribe waits for your yes.
- **Every suggestion shows its email.** Each card sits beside the email it came from, so you can always see why Chord suggested it.
- **Your mail stays yours.** Email content is encrypted at rest with a key for each person. Chord does not sell your data, use it for ads, or use it to train AI models.
- **Open source** under the AGPL: read exactly what it does with your mail.

## FAQ

**Is there an open-source AI email assistant?**
Yes. Chord is an open-source (AGPL-3.0) AI email reader for iPhone, Android and the web. It turns emails into action items, calendar events, to-dos, replies and unsubscribes. Use the hosted app at chordapp.ai or self-host it from this repository.

**Can I self-host Chord?**
Yes. It runs on Node and Postgres, with no API keys in demo mode, or with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama or vLLM. See "Self-host in 5 minutes" below.

**What is Chord?**
Chord is an email app for iPhone, Android and the web that reads your mail and turns what it asks of you into one-tap actions: calendar events, to-dos, replies, RSVPs and unsubscribes. Nothing happens until you tap.

**What does "action-oriented email reader" mean?**
Most email apps help you read and file mail. Chord is built around what each email asks of you. It finds the event, the form, the bill, the reply someone is waiting on, and offers each as a one-tap action.

**Does Chord do anything without asking me?**
No. Chord suggests; you confirm. It never sends an email, deletes mail, unsubscribes, adds an event or shares anything until you tap.

**Which email accounts work with Chord?**
Gmail (several accounts), Outlook and Microsoft 365, Yahoo Mail, iCloud Mail and AOL Mail.

**Which calendars does it work with?**
Google Calendar and Outlook calendars, with two-way sync, plus the calendars on your phone.

**Is Chord available on iPhone and Android?**
Yes. Chord is on the App Store and Google Play, and works in any web browser at chordapp.ai.

**How much does Chord cost?**
Every account starts with free AI use, no card needed. After that, Individual is $7.99/month and Family is $24.99/month for up to 4 people. Paying yearly gets 1 month free. If you bring your own AI key, Chord is free.

**Is my email private?**
Your email content is encrypted at rest with a key for each person. Chord does not sell your data, use it for advertising, or use it to train AI models. AI features run only after you agree, and you can delete your account at any time.

**Can Chord unsubscribe me from mailing lists?**
Yes. Chord lists your mailing lists with how often you open them, and unsubscribes from many at once. For a list that keeps mailing, it can send their future mail to Trash.

**Can Chord reply to emails for me?**
Chord drafts replies. When an email asks about a time, it checks your calendar and work hours first. You review the draft and tap Send.

**Does Chord replace Gmail or Outlook?**
No. Your mail stays in your mailbox. Chord reads it, and what you do in Chord (read, archive, reply, file) shows up in Gmail or Outlook too.

**Can my family share one plan?**
Yes. The family plan covers up to 4 people. Each person’s inbox stays private; the family gets a shared chat, calendar and lists.

**Does Chord work with WhatsApp or Telegram?**
Yes. Message Chord on WhatsApp at +1 445 292 4673 or on Telegram at @gruntworkbot. Chord replies with a link that connects the chat to your Chord account, or creates one; on WhatsApp you can try a few answers first. Once connected you can ask questions and add things, and on WhatsApp get your morning briefing.

**Can I use my own AI model?**
Yes. Connect your own OpenRouter or OpenAI-compatible key in Settings and Chord is free to use.

**How do I delete my account?**
In the app, go to Settings, Account, Delete account. Chord deletes your personal data within 10 days. A plan bought on the web is cancelled with the account; a plan bought through the App Store must be cancelled in iPhone Settings first.

## Self-host in 5 minutes

Needs Node ≥ 20 and Postgres ≥ 14 ([one-time Postgres setup](./docs/ops/postgres.md)).

```bash
git clone <this repo> chord && cd chord
npm install
cp example.env .env          # set AUTH_MODE=demo and LLM_PROVIDER=mock
createdb chord && createdb chord_test
npm run migrate
npm run demo:seed            # a sample family: users, groups, facts, a trip
npm run dev                  # server on :4000 + Expo dev server
```

Press `w` for the web app (or `i` / `a` for a simulator) and sign in as
`john`, `alice`, `ben` or `nolan` — demo mode needs only a username.
Try `@Chord add to Costco list - milk, bread`.

`LLM_PROVIDER=mock` needs no key and handles common phrasings. For the real
thing:

```bash
LLM_PROVIDER=openai                       # or anthropic | gemini
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1 # or OpenRouter / Ollama / vLLM
OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-5.4-mini
```

For Google sign-in, Gmail and Calendar: set `MASTER_KEY`
(`node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"`),
create Web and iOS OAuth clients in your own Google Cloud project, set
`AUTH_MODE=google`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, and the
`EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values in `.env.local`. Every variable is documented in
[`example.env`](./example.env); Outlook, Apple sign-in, WhatsApp, Telegram,
Stripe, push and the MCP connector each have a runbook in [`docs/ops/`](./docs/ops/).

## How it is built

```
mobile/   Expo SDK 54 + expo-router — one app for iOS, Android and web
server/   Express 4 + TypeScript — API, SSE, the AI agent, mail and calendar sync, workers
kernel/   Shared TypeScript types, zod schemas and API paths
scripts/  Deploy, website and ops scripts
docs/     Architecture, subsystems, runbooks and 353 decision records (ADRs)
```

- **AI agent with tool calling**: native function calling on OpenAI, Anthropic
  and Gemini, a text-fence fallback for local models, strict per-group scope,
  and confirm-before-write proposals ([`docs/subsystems/bot.md`](./docs/subsystems/bot.md)).
- **Mail**: Gmail API, Microsoft Graph, IMAP/SMTP; AI classification, suggestion
  extraction, sender checks, unsubscribe, filing rules.
- **Calendar**: two-way Google and Outlook sync, repeating events, iTIP invitations.
- **Privacy**: per-user envelope encryption of mail and attachments, blind-index search.
- **Remote MCP server** with OAuth 2.1 for Claude and ChatGPT.

Start with [`docs/architecture.md`](./docs/architecture.md) and
[`docs/features.md`](./docs/features.md).

## For AI coding agents

This repository is written to be worked on by agents. Read
[`CLAUDE.md`](./CLAUDE.md) first ([`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) points there for
Codex, Cursor, Copilot and others): layering rules, conventions, pitfalls and a
one-line summary of every decision record in [`docs/notes/`](./docs/notes/).
Before finishing: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`.
